messages:
ravi (Design): Pushed a variant of the Rules preview panel that includes a mini timeline for precedence visualization. Link: https://internal.redwood.dev/preview/precedence-timeline

ben (Product): Love the timeline. Quick ask: can the simulator show which rule fired for a sample request inline so we can debug precedence?

noor (Eng): We can add a 'why this rule' line in the simulator output. Right now the simulator uses a cached index of rules which might cause stale results after rapid edits.

ravi (Design): Also noticed the validation toast says 'Rule conflict' which is a bit scary. Maybe 'Priority overlap' or 'Order mismatch' would be friendlier.

ben (Product): +1 for softer copy. 'Priority overlap — review the rules highlighted below' maybe.

ella (A11y): For the timeline, each node needs an accessible name (e.g., 'Priority 1 — catch-all') and keyboard focus. Add aria-describedby linking to the rule detail region.

noor (Eng): Will wire aria-describedby. Also we'll change simulator to invalidate cache on save and re-run simulation automatically when the ruleset changes.

ravi (Design): Microcopy suggestion under the simulate button: 'Runs your current ruleset against sample traffic. Simulator may take 1–2s after edits.' Helps set expectation.

ben (Product): Found another tiny UX bug: when reordering quickly, the UI shows a toast 'Order conflict' then auto-resolves. It feels alarm-y. Can we turn that into an inline warning row rather than a global toast?

noor (Eng): I'll stop showing toasts for transient optimistic conflicts and add a subtle inline banner in the table header if there's an unresolved reorder error.

ella (A11y): Re: drag handles — make them focusable buttons with 'aria-grabbed' and announce 'picked up' / 'dropped' to assistive tech. Also ensure contrast of the timeline colors meets AA when used as conveyance.

preview-bot: Screenshot uploaded: precedence-timeline.png

ravi (Design): Small copy tweak request: change rule weight label from 'Priority' to 'Order (1 = first)'. New users get confused by whether 1 is lowest or highest.

ben (Product): Good call. Clarifying parenthetical saves confusion. Update product docs too.

noor (Eng): Will implement the copy change and the debounce for reorder events (400ms). Also adding a 'last-simulated-at' timestamp to the simulator so you can see whether results are from fresh data.

ravi (Design): Thanks — if you can push the copy + the 'why this rule' line, I'll re-run the accessibility pass and pick between two color palettes for the timeline contrast.

ella (A11y): I'll follow up with specific contrast numbers and suggested aria labels. Thanks team. :)
